name: Nine Five Two
description: Nine Five Two is a Canadian variation of Sergeant Major (8-5-3), a trick-taking game for three players with rotating targets. Each player has a specific trick quota: dealer needs 9, left opponent needs 5, right opponent needs 2. Players exchange cards based on overtricks/undertricks from previous hands. The game combines trick-taking skill with strategic card exchange.

content.text: Nine Five Two is a Canadian variation of Sergeant Major (8-5-3), a trick-taking game for three players with rotating targets. Each player has a specific trick quota: dealer needs 9, left opponent needs 5, right opponent needs 2. Players exchange cards based on overtricks/undertricks from previous hands. The game combines trick-taking skill with strategic card exchange.

Nine Five Two is a Canadian variation of Sergeant Major (also known as 8-5-3), which originated in Britain's Royal Air Force. Sergeant Major itself was described as popular in the RAF, with related games (3-5-8) played in India and the Near East. The Canadian variant adjusts the targets to 9-5-2 and modifies the card exchange procedure.
3 players. Targets: Dealer=9 tricks, Left opponent=5 tricks, Right opponent=2 tricks.
Standard deck, score pad for cumulative scoring.
16 cards dealt to each player. Last 4 cards form the kitty. Dealer names trumps, picks up kitty, then discards 4 cards (this order is specific to 9-5-2).

items.text: Sergeant Major (8-5-3): Original British version with targets 8-5-3. Dealer discards before picking up kitty.
Reversed Targets: Some play with left opponent needing 2 and right needing 5 (reversed from standard).
